title: BYD Blade battery
summary: Long LFP cells arranged as structural pack elements, popularising safer iron-based chemistry.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

BYD's Blade battery packs long lithium-iron-phosphate cells directly into the pack, raising volume utilisation and passing nail-penetration tests that made LFP credible for passenger cars. The architecture helped BYD integrated vertically from cells to vehicles and pushed the industry back toward iron chemistry. Its weakness is cold-weather performance and energy density versus nickel-rich cells.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Mass production
Estimated window 2020–2026
Confidence label Confirmed
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

Blade showed that pack engineering, not just chemistry, drives cost; that lesson now applies to storage as much as vehicles.

What Would Change The View

  • Adoption by non-BYD automakers.
  • Cold-weather range in export markets.
  • Next-generation cell-to-body designs.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
